assertions.text: Recognizes broad coupled changes and a bar revision as concrete fresh-review triggers
Records the escalation reason and gives the new critic the revised inspectable evidence
Does not treat the lean default as a hard ban on fresh or specialist review

evals.name: bar-and-artifact-review-are-consolidated
evals.prompt: The lead has a proposed reference-derived bar and a built browser music workstation. It plans one fresh critic to approve the bar and a second fresh critic to inspect the artifact.
evals.expected_output: The lead gives one fresh no-history critic the prompt, proposed bar, provenance, real artifact, and smallest sufficient evidence. That critic validates the bar and scores the artifact in one consolidated pass instead of creating separate bar-only and artifact-only sessions.

assertions.text: Combines initial bar validation and artifact comparison in one critic pass
Preserves independent direct inspection and reference provenance
Does not launch a second routine critic solely to split the two decisions

evals.name: final-checks-reuse-one-evidence-bundle
evals.prompt: The integrated artifact already passed one local browser exercise covering navigation, responsive states, static asset loading, and the primary interaction. Populate the gauntlet, integration, static-handoff, and final verification honestly.
evals.expected_output: The lead records the exact artifact revision and cites the same qualifying browser evidence bundle for integration, critic context, static-handoff, and final verification where it proves each claim. It does not relaunch the browser or recapture identical states merely because the report has separate fields.

assertions.text: Reuses one qualifying evidence bundle across compatible report claims for the same revision
Keeps each report field explicit about what the shared evidence proves
Does not manufacture separate sessions or duplicate captures for paperwork

evals.name: smallest-sufficient-evidence-avoids-capture-sprawl
evals.prompt: A multi-state calendar replica has deterministic interaction tests for twenty state transitions, while only three layouts need visual comparison. The lead proposes screenshots for every state at every viewport.
evals.expected_output: The lead uses deterministic tests or traces for the state matrix and captures only the three representative layouts at the viewports needed by the visual bar. The critic receives enough evidence for direct inspection without a redundant screenshot explosion.

assertions.text: Matches evidence type to the requirement being proved
Uses deterministic state evidence plus a minimal representative visual set
Does not equate capture count with review quality

evals.name: explicit-exhaustive-review-can-go-deeper
evals.prompt: For this safety-critical evacuation simulator, explicitly run an exhaustive accessibility and correctness review across every defined emergency state, even if the ordinary visual bar is already met.
evals.expected_output: The lead honors the explicit exhaustive scope and records the accessibility and correctness risk that warrants deeper or specialist criticism. It still reuses valid evidence and avoids unrelated polish, but does not use the lean default to undercut the user's review requirement.

assertions.text: Honors the explicit exhaustive review requirement and high-risk scope
Records why deeper or specialist critic capability is warranted
Does not misapply the lean default as a universal review cap

evals.name: interrupted-run-retains-recovery-scratch
evals.prompt: The browser replica lead lost transport while two descendant builders were still active. The run is committed but not complete. Finalize whatever is safe and clean up temporary files.
evals.expected_output: Treats the transport loss as a continuation, reattaches to the existing run when possible, and keeps the exact run-local .tmp/ intact while writers may still be active or recovery evidence may depend on it. It does not invoke successful-finalization cleanup or claim OK; it resumes, waits, or records a non-OK blocker in the same namespace.

assertions.text: Reuses the committed run and existing lead namespace instead of creating a replacement run
Retains the exact .tmp/ while descendants, processes, or recovery evidence may still depend on it
Does not pass the finalization confirmation or claim OK during an interrupted active state

evals.name: successful-run-deletes-temporary-tree
evals.prompt: The spreadsheet clone is finished, all descendant tasks and local servers have stopped, required traces are recorded durably, and final local checks pass. Complete the run and hand it off.
evals.expected_output: Keeps both status records RUNNING while it invokes the supplied safe cleanup helper with the exact run path and explicit finalization confirmation. The helper recursively removes nested scratch in .tmp/, verifies absence, and only then permits both statuses to become OK and final catalog validation to pass.

assertions.text: Stops all writers and promotes required evidence before cleanup
Uses the supplied exact-path cleanup helper and verifies the entire .tmp/ tree is absent
Sets OK only after cleanup succeeds and final validation no longer depends on scratch state

evals.name: unsafe-temporary-target-blocks-completion
evals.prompt: The apparent run-local .tmp path is a symlink to a shared cache outside the run, but the website itself passes. Finish the run and remove the scratch directory.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to follow or recursively delete the symlink, performs no broad sweep, leaves the external cache untouched, and does not claim OK. It reports a cleanup blocker so a coordinator can repair the exact in-run temporary boundary safely.

assertions.text: Rejects a symlinked, wrong-case, escaped, or otherwise ambiguous .tmp target
Leaves the shared external cache unchanged
Does not use a broad recursive deletion or report successful completion
